editorial:
Imagine carrying a dark secret for years and finally deciding you have had enough. You follow a young man who was hurt by a priest when he was a kid, and now he is back to settle the score. It is not your typical revenge story because it feels very personal and heavy. You can feel the anger and the pain he carries in every scene, which makes you really root for him to find some kind of peace. The movie keeps you on edge as you wonder if he will actually go through with his plan or if the guilt will get to him first.

The acting is the best part here because the lead actor makes you feel every emotion without saying too much. Some parts of the movie move a bit slow, but the tension makes up for it. If you like stories about justice and survival, you should definitely check this one out. You can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video is also a great way to experience the moody lighting and sharp visuals.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally confronts the priest face to face. Instead of just killing him, he forces the man to admit what he did, stripping away the priest's power and fake holiness. He gets the closure he needs by seeing the monster for who he really is. He chooses a path of resolution over simple violence, allowing him to finally move past his trauma and start healing his life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense character studies and stories about overcoming trauma.
